To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dengue outbreaks in New Caledonian were due to the introduction of viruses of genotype I and IV, but only genotype I viruses were responsible for the 2012–13 outbreak.

the epidemiological and molecular features associated with the recent DENV-1 epidemic in New Caledonian are unique and that the DENV-4 epidemic that followed was likely due to a single introduction of a DENV-4 virus from Asia.

the 2012–13 dengue virus 1 (DENV-1) outbreak in New Caledonian (NC) occurred in the context of a genotype I virus introduction and that this genotype replaced the previously circulating genotype IV virus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epidemiology and evolution of the dengue serotypes in NC and the Pacific.
the epidemiological and molecular characterization of dengue viruses circulating in NC
the epidemiology of denv-1 in new caledonia, south pacific, 2001-2013.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DENV-4 outbreak in 2008 may have contributed to a reduction of the immune response to the subsequent DENV-1 infection in 2012–13.
the epidemiology of denv-1 in New caledonia has been characterized by introductions of denv- 1 genotype I and IV viruses, and the occurrence of a genotype switch during the 2012-2013 outbreak.
NC has experienced three DENV-1 introductions in the last decade, with the most recent being from South-east Asia, which is a new source for this serotype in the Pacific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-1 genotypes circulating in NC were imported from the Pacific and that DENV-4 was imported from Asia.

the DENV-4 outbreak in NC was likely a consequence of the co-circulation of genotype I and IV DENV-1 strains, and the DENV-IV strain likely replaced the DENV-I genotype I strain in the population, which then led to a DENV-IV epidemic.

NC has experienced three DENV-1 epidemics over the last decade, the first one was due to viruses of genotype IV, the second one due to a mixture of genotypes I and IV and the third one due to viruses of only genotype I.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DENV-1 is circulating again in NC, and the virus has a South-east Asian origin, which is a new feature in the Pacific.
the DENV-4 epidemic in 2008 may have played a significant role in the emergence of DENV-1 genotype I in 2012, as the DENV-3 epidemic did in the emergence of the genotype IV in 2001.
the DENV-2–4 viruses that circulated in the Pacific in 2012 were likely introduced from South-east Asia.
